h2: Villa Maintenance Jimbaran – Plumbing & Pool Care
intro: Living between the bay and the Bukit means your villa faces salt-laden air, fluctuating water pressure, and mineral-heavy supply year-round. Our Villa Maintenance Jimbaran service covers plumbing, pool systems, pumps, water heaters, and roof checks so small issues never become costly repairs. Whether you manage a family villa in Kedonganan or an owner's home up in Bukit Jimbaran, regular check-ups keep everything running smoothly.

sections.h3: Salt Air, Hard Water, and Hillside Pressure
sections.text: Bay-side homes take a real hit from chloride in the air—copper fittings, pump housings, and pool ladders corrode noticeably faster than inland. Up on the Bukit, villas depend on overhead tanks and booster pumps; low pressure and constant cycling wear seals quickly. The hard water here also leaves calcium scale inside mixers, heater elements, and filter cartridges. A quarterly inspection catches all three problems before they cause leaks or equipment failure.

sections.h3: What a Regular Check-Up Covers Here
sections.text: For owners and managers, each visit follows a structured checklist: drain valves, overflow pipes, pump seals, heater descaling, pool chemistry balance, and roof flashings—especially critical ahead of the October-to-March monsoon. We also run pre-arrival checks so the property is ready when guests land. After every visit you receive a written report with photos, flagged items, and recommended next steps, which keeps owner reporting simple and transparent.

Send us a few photos of the issue—a leaking fitting, cloudy pool water, a pump that keeps tripping—and a short note about where it sits in the villa. Mention your area (Goa Gong, Kedonganan, or up on the hill) and whether the property faces the coast; that changes which parts are most likely affected. Pricing depends on the specific job, so once we see the photos we'll give you a clear quote right there on WhatsApp before any work begins.

sections.h3: Small Habits That Save Big Repairs
sections.text: Rinse outdoor fittings and pool ladders with fresh water after heavy sea-spray days, particularly for homes facing the bay. Flush tank lines monthly if pressure drops below normal, and inspect pump seals every two months rather than waiting for a visible leak. Descale water heaters and mixers at least twice a year to counter the mineral load. Before the first monsoon rains, walk the roofline and clear gutters—water pooling on a Bukit slope can find its way under tiles fast.

faq.q: How often should I schedule maintenance for a Jimbaran villa?
faq.a: A quarterly visit suits most properties well, but bay-side villas with pools may benefit from a check every six to eight weeks because of constant salt exposure.

faq.q: Do you handle both plumbing and pool equipment in one visit?
faq.a: Yes—we cover pumps, filters, heaters, mixers, drains, and roof flashings in a single inspection, so you get one consolidated report instead of juggling multiple trades.

faq.q: What should I include when messaging you on WhatsApp?
faq.a: Photos of the problem area, your neighbourhood name, and whether the villa sits near the coast or up on the hill; that's enough for us to assess the likely cause and send a quote.
